heroHeadline: Day 682: Peso Strengthens to 16.98/USD as US Declines Full USMCA Extension; Mexico's Colombia Earthquake Aid Effort Hits Certification Snag; AMLO's Son Says US Revoked His Visa
heroSubtitle: August 14, 2026 marks Day 682 of Claudia Sheinbaum's presidency. The peso strengthened to 16.98 per US dollar, with Sheinbaum citing delayed public works now breaking ground as reason to expect accelerating H2 2026 growth; she also confirmed a weekend Tamaulipas tour to inaugurate two new hospitals. On the USMCA front, the July 1 deadline passed without a clean 16-year renewal — the U.S. formally declined to extend the agreement in its current form, triggering rolling annual joint reviews under Article 34.7.4; Round 3 talks in Mexico City (late July) resolved the 'vast majority' of the U.S.'s original 54-item concern list per Economy Secretary Ebrard, with Round 4 set for Washington in September. Mexico's diplomatic energy this week centered on Colombia: after an August 10 7.4-magnitude earthquake in Chocó department, Sheinbaum readied a 255-strong military relief brigade (Agrupamiento Cali) and pledged 'all the support' Colombia needs, but Bogotá ultimately barred the Mexican rescue brigade over a missing certification — Mexico instead delivered 58.5 tonnes of humanitarian aid by air. Separately, Mexico and Peru restored diplomatic relations on August 7 as former Peruvian PM Betssy Chávez, who had been sheltering in Mexico's Lima embassy, flew to Mexico City under a safe-conduct pass. On August 13, Andrés Manuel 'Andy' López Beltrán, son of former president AMLO, said the U.S. State Department revoked his visa, calling it political retaliation — adding pressure on the Sheinbaum government amid a separate PAN-flagged fuel-theft investigation referencing him. Inflation continued cooling to 3.12% in July (lowest since May 2020), and approval sits at 57% (Aug 6 AtlasIntel), up from a summer low, as Banxico's policy rate held at 6.50% for a second straight meeting.
